newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - Telefonos de Mexico rises.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - Telefonos de Mexico rises.

text.p: Telefonos de Mexico rose Tuesday, boosted by a new economic development plan from the Mexican government, traders said.

American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) in the Mexican phone company, also known as Telmex, were up 3/4 to 25-3/8 in early afternoon. Volume was moderate at 1.7 million shares and the company was on the New York Stock Exchange most-active list.
Traders said Telmex was being helped by President Ernesto Zedillo's announcement of a economic development plan to run through the year 2000.
Zedillo predicted yearly economic growth of five percent and said May inflation would be lower than the 1.08 percent recorded in April.

"During the last couple of weeks banks have been moving their asset allocations to Mexico out of other countries in Latin America," a trader said. "They see inflation coming down and Mexico taking the proper fiscal steps."
Also, after the market's close Monday, Telmex said it would recoup $422 million in local telephone investment from holders of long-distance concessions.
Among other Mexican stocks, glass maker Vitro SA rose 3/8 to 9-1/8.
Argentine oil company YPF rose 1/2 to 30-3/4 in moderate volume. Traders said the ADRs were bolstered by the company's plan to float 10 percent of its share capital.
Among European shares, oil and telecommunications companies strengthened.
Royal Dutch Petroleum Co rose 5/8 to 195-5/8 and France's Total SA was up 1/2 at 45-7/8.
Swedish telecommunication equipment company Telefon AB L.M. Ericsson rose 5/8 to 36-1/4, and Finland's Nokia Group was up one to 67-1/2.
Advancers led decliners 286 to 212 among 814 ADRs. The ADR group was up 0.33 percent and volume was 45 million ADRs.
ADRs allow U.S. trade of foreign shares.
